claim: two builds of the recipe in different directories under different names are byte-identical
the per-step hash lists of the two runs are identical (31 states)
every step leaves a different file, so a hash names exactly one step
recipe.StepHashes (the cached list later chapters use) equals the list just built
recipe.MatchStep names the step a database equals
the rollback-mode recipe also rebuilds byte for byte at every step
SQL random() makes two runs differ
current_timestamp makes runs differ once the wall clock's second changes (its resolution is one second, so two fast runs can still match)
FINDING: an unordered INSERT ... SELECT run twice on the same build with the same plan gives identical files
an unordered INSERT ... SELECT changes the file when the scan order changes; ORDER BY removes the dependence
FINDING: in WAL mode on one connection with secure_delete=ON, different transaction batches give identical files
with secure_delete=OFF different batches differ, and only in bytes no cell uses (stale content left in unallocated space, freeblocks or freelist pages)
in rollback mode different batches differ, and with secure_delete=ON only in the change counter (it counts commits)
secure_delete=FAST is not ON: on the same history FAST leaves old bytes in the unused space of freelist pages that ON zeroes
rowid assignment past the maximum rowid makes two runs differ
FINDING: in WAL mode the number of connection sessions changes the file, and only the change counter (bytes 24-27 and 92-95)
in rollback mode the number of connection sessions does not change the file
in WAL mode only a commit that writes page 1 writes the change counter: sessions whose commits never touch page 1 leave the file identical
WAL mode: a rolled-back SAVEPOINT changes the committed file even with secure_delete=ON: reused freelist leaf pages keep the rolled-back bytes, and page 1's change counter moves
rollback mode: a rolled-back SAVEPOINT leaves the rolled-back bytes in reused freelist leaf pages (secure_delete=ON does not clear them)
